schema: voyage-tce-model seed: market conventions and the rules the engine implements

items.rule: TCE = (gross freight + other revenue - commissions - voyage costs) / total voyage days, net of commissions; voyage costs are bunkers, port charges, canal tolls, ETS allowances, war risk premiums and other voyage specific costs, never operating or capital costs.
items.source: Baltic Exchange, Guide to Market Benchmarks v8.8, Appendix 3, page 98
quote: The Baltic publishes Time Charter Equivalent values for various voyage route assessments. These are published as a net value.
Additional expenses particular to the trade, such as but not limited to, additional insurance, cleaning costs, security guards and emission costs.

items.rule: Sea days = distance x (1 + 5 percent weather margin) / (speed x 24), laden and ballast; plus port, waiting and canal days from the TCE route description. The ballast leg runs from the TCE delivery port (the discharge port) back to the load port.
items.source: GMB v8.8 Appendix 3, pages 98 and 99
quote: 5% weather allowance
Distance from the starting place named in the TCE description to the Load port.

items.rule: Fuel is priced at the main bunkering port closest to the load port, in the grade the activity burns. The guide changed its description of the fuel price in version 8.4 (May 2026), so how the Baltic priced fuel before then is not documented in the current guide.
items.source: GMB v8.8 Appendix 3, page 98, and the document history
quote: The cost of the fuel at the main bunkering port closest to the load port.
May 2026 - Update to description in appendix 3 on FuelPrice

items.rule: The Baltic's tanker TCEs include port and canal costs supplied by Cory Brothers, which are not published; the study takes them as lump sum inputs.
items.source: GMB v8.8 Appendix 3, page 98
items.quote: Port costs supplied by Cory Brothers Shipping

items.rule: USD/t = WS / 100 x flat rate (the route's flat rate for the year, set by the Worldscale Association and licensed); a lump sum is divided by the cargo.
items.source: GMB v8.8 Appendix 3, page 98
quote: Worldscale assessment would be converted to $/mt by applying the applicable flat rate.
A lumpsum assessment would be divided by the loaded cargo quantity.

items.rule: Baltic tanker routes are assessed on 3.75 percent total commission, since circular 27/21. The guide states the total, address commission and brokerage together, and asks its panellists to allow for business quoted at other rates, such as a higher or lower address commission; the study takes the total as one input, since only the total moves the TCE and no public source gives a typical split.
items.source: GMB v8.8, document history, version 4.7, and section 7.3.3(5), page 34
quote: As per Circular 27/21 all tanker routes were changed to standard commission at 3.75% (from 2.5%)
Panellists are expected to make allowance for any variation in the rate of commission, for example increased or reduced address commissions

items.rule: Baltic dry voyage routes and trips are assessed on 5 percent total commission.
items.source: GMB v8.8 Appendix 2, route descriptions (C3, page 77)
items.quote: 6 hrs turn time at loading port, 24 hrs turn time at discharge port. Age max 18 yrs. 5% total commission.

items.rule: 0.50 percent sulphur worldwide and 0.10 percent inside an emission control area.
items.source: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14.1 and 14.4, resolution MEPC.328(76)
quote: The sulphur content of fuel oil used or carried for use on board a ship shall not exceed 0.50% m/m.
While a ship is operating within an emission control area, the sulphur content of fuel oil used on board that ship shall not exceed 0.10% m/m.

items.rule: In force 1 May 2024; under regulation 14.7 ships are exempt for twelve months, so the 0.10 percent limit applies from 1 May 2025.
items.source: Resolution MEPC.361(79)
items.quote: the said amendments shall enter into force on 1 May 2024 upon their acceptance

items.rule: Ships at berth in EU ports burn fuel of at most 0.10 percent sulphur.
items.source: Directive (EU) 2016/802, Article 7
items.quote: Member States shall take all necessary measures to ensure that ships at berth in Union ports do not use marine fuels with a sulphur content exceeding 0,10% by mass

items.rule: Tonnes of CO2 per tonne of fuel: HFO (ISO 8217 RME to RMK) 3.114, LFO (RMA to RMD) 3.151, MDO and MGO (DMX to DMB) 3.206; CH4 0.00005 and N2O 0.00018 g per g.
items.source: Regulation (EU) 2015/757 Annex I as replaced by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2776
items.quote: HFO ISO 8217 Grades RME to RMK 3,114 0,00005 0,00018 - LFO ISO 8217 Grades RMA to RMD 3,151 0,00005 0,00018 - MDO MGO ISO 8217 Grades DMX to DMB 3,206 0,00005 0,00018
items.display: HFO, ISO 8217 Grades RME to RMK: CO2 3,114, CH4 0,00005, N2O 0,00018; LFO, Grades RMA to RMD: CO2 3,151, CH4 0,00005, N2O 0,00018; MDO and MGO, Grades DMX to DMB: CO2 3,206, CH4 0,00005, N2O 0,00018 (grams per gram of fuel; the column heads are images in the regulation's text)

items.rule: CH4 28 and N2O 265.
items.source: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1044, Annex

items.rule: VLSFO is classed as HFO (ISO 8217 residual grades RME, RMG and RMK) for its emission factor.
items.source: IMO resolution MEPC.391(81), 2024 LCA guidelines, Appendix 1
items.quote: (ISO 8217 Grades RME, RMG and RMK, 0.10 < S
items.display: Heavy Fuel Oil (VLSFO) (ISO 8217 Grades RME, RMG and RMK, 0.10 < S <= 0.50%)

items.rule: 50 percent of emissions on voyages into or out of an EU port, 100 percent between EU ports and within a port of call.
items.source: Directive 2003/87/EC Article 3ga, inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/959
items.quote: fifty percent (50%) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State

items.rule: Allowances for 40 percent of 2024 emissions, 70 percent of 2025 and 100 percent from 2026.
items.source: Directive 2003/87/EC Article 3gb
items.quote: (a) 40% of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (b) 70% of verified emissions reported for 2025

items.rule: Shipping's allowances cover carbon dioxide, and methane and nitrous oxide from 2026.
items.source: Directive 2003/87/EC Annex I, maritime transport row (consolidated text of 1 March 2024)
items.quote: Carbon dioxide From 1 January 2026, methane and nitrous oxide

items.rule: The charterer provides and pays for the allowances for the ship's emissions during the charter and transfers them to the owner's account: on a trip time charter the trip's allowances are the charterer's.
items.source: BIMCO ETS Allowances Clause for Time Charter Parties 2022, clauses (c)(i) and (c)(iii)
quote: Throughout the Charter Party period the Charterers shall provide and pay for the Emission Allowances corresponding to the Vessel's emissions under the scope of the applicable Emission Scheme
the party providing and paying for the fuel under the time charter is the party that is responsible for providing and paying for emissions trading allowances
shall be transferred by the Charterers and received into the Owners

items.rule: The shipping company surrenders the allowances, whoever bears their cost under the charter.
items.source: Directive 2003/87/EC Article 3gc (consolidated text of 1 March 2024)
items.quote: The shipping company shall remain the entity responsible for surrendering allowances

items.rule: Limit 91.16 gCO2e/MJ less 2 percent from 2025; penalty = |compliance balance| / (GHG intensity x 41,000) x 2,400 EUR; assessed on the ship's yearly average, so the study shows one voyage's share and keeps it out of the TCE unless chosen.
items.source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 4(2) and Annex IV Part B; Annex II factors
quote: reducing the reference value of 91,16 grams of CO 2 equivalent per MJ by the following percentage: - 2% from 1 January 2025
Is 1 metric ton of VLSFO that is equivalent to 41 000 MJ 7. 2 400
HFO ISO 8217 Grades RME to RMK 0,0405 13,5 ALL ICEs 3,114 0,00005 0,00018
display: reducing the reference value of 91,16 grams of CO2 equivalent per MJ by the following percentage: 2% from 1 January 2025
41 000: 1 metric ton of VLSFO is equivalent to 41 000 MJ; 2 400: the amount paid in EUR per equivalent metric ton of VLSFO

HFO, ISO 8217 Grades RME to RMK: lower calorific value 0,0405 MJ per g; well to tank 13,5 gCO2eq per MJ; all ICEs; CO2 3,114, CH4 0,00005, N2O 0,00018 g per g of fuel (the column heads are images in the text)

items.rule: FuelEU takes CH4 25 and N2O 298, the values of the Renewable Energy Directive, not the ETS's 28 and 265.
items.source: Directive (EU) 2018/2001 Annex V Part C point 4
items.quote: those gases shall be valued as follows: 2 CO: 1 2 N O: 298 2 CH: 25
items.display: those gases shall be valued as follows: CO2: 1, N2O: 298, CH4: 25

items.rule: An additional war risk premium is a percentage of hull and machinery value, charged on entering a listed area for a period of up to seven days there; each further seven days inside, or part of them, is another period. Cover periods have shortened since February 2026, so the count is a lower bound.
items.source: Platts, 1 April 2026 and 5 October 2026, republished by Hellenic Shipping News
items.quote: The AWRP had reached around 2.5% of the Hull and Machinery value of ships per seven-day period in the Persian Gulf earlier in March

items.topic: Who pays the war risk premium
items.rule: On spot voyage charters the premium is usually the charterer's. The study leaves it out of the owner's TCE, as the Baltic's TCEs leave it out, and shows it as the charterer's cost; the payer input moves it into the owner's costs for a fixture that puts it in the freight.
items.source: Platts, 8 December 2025, republished by Hellenic Shipping News
items.quote: AWRPs are usually on the charterer's account in spot freight deals

items.rule: The owner is reimbursed the additional premium through the charter chain; the clause covers a deviation to avoid a dangerous place but not waiting time, which stays the owner's.
items.source: Gard, 21 March 2026, republished by Hellenic Shipping News
quote: the cost of any additional premiums will flow through the charterparty chain
VOYWAR 2013 only addresses the cost of a deviation to avoid a dangerous place, not waiting time
